title: Gladly API
snippet:
At Gladly, we believe that customer service is best when it's a conversation. That means more than just helping customers with one-off questions or issues: it's about making them feel known, valued, and respected for the individuals they are.
The Gladly API was built to help facilitate those relationships, providing agents with the rich customer context they need to deliver seamless experiences that make customers feel like they're more than just a number in a sea of others.
# Overview
You can integrate easily with Gladly by calling Gladly's REST API and implementing the Lookup API to provide data from your own services.

Clients can access the **REST API** via HTTPS at your organization's Gladly domain (e.g. `https://{organization}.gladly.com`).
Resources follow REST semantics and utilize industry-standard HTTP verbs, response codes, and authentication schemes.

[here](https://help.gladly.com/developer/docs/lookup-adapter-introduction).

title: Chatwoot vs Gladly: Person-Centered Support (2026)
snippet:
Transparent Pricing
# Person-centered support with transparent pricing and messaging channels included
Gladly pioneered person-centered support with a single conversation timeline per customer. Chatwoot offers the same unified customer view with 12+ channels, an AI agent and copilot, and pricing that doesn't require an enterprise sales call.
- Unified customer conversation history across all channels
- Transparent per-agent pricing, no enterprise-only access
- Captain AI agent and copilot on paid plans
- 12+ channels including WhatsApp, Instagram, Telegram, and more
- Open source with self-hosting. Gladly is cloud-only

- ### Enterprise-only pricing
Gladly requires a custom sales call for pricing and typically targets large enterprises. Chatwoot has transparent pricing from free to $99/agent/mo.
- ### No free or starter tier
Gladly has no free plan or self-service signup. Chatwoot lets you start free and scale up as needed.
- ### Closed platform
Gladly offers APIs and integrations, but the platform itself is closed. Chatwoot's open API, webhooks, and source code give you full control.

- ### Transparent pricing
Free plan for small teams, paid plans from $19/agent/mo. No sales calls required, no hidden costs.

title: Gladly MCP server for Claude & ChatGPT | usefulapi
snippet:
## Pricing
| Plan | Price | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 50 tool calls / month |
| Pro | $9/mo · $90/yr | Unlimited* |
*Pro fair use limit: 10,000 tool calls a month on this server. For more, write to [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#b0c3c5c0c0dfc2c4f0c5c3d5d6c5dcd1c0d99ed9df).
Pro covers this Gladly server only. Subscribe with `gladly_upgrade` (it returns a Stripe Checkout link). Cancel any time with `gladly_cancel_subscription`: Pro continues to the end of the paid period, with no refund for the current period, and running `gladly_upgrade` before then undoes the cancel. Or write to [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#63101613130c11172316100605160f02130a4d0a0c).

- **Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)**`gladly_upgrade`
Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Gladly (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically.

What does it cost?
The Free plan gives 50 tool calls / month. Pro costs $9/mo or $90/yr, with unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 tool calls a month), for this Gladly server only. Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period. Run `gladly_usage_status` to see how many calls you used.
